Role Overview

This role sits between our legal reality and our readers. CookieYes publishes a large library of privacy content that businesses across the world rely on to understand what the law asks of them, and we need someone professionally qualified to stand behind it.

We are looking for a law graduate who writes because they want to, not because a brief demanded it. You will track privacy legislation across jurisdictions, translate it into content our customers can act on, and act as the internal check on the legal accuracy of everything we publish and ship. Part of the role is genuine legal work: reviewing our own agreements, supporting compliance queries from customers, and keeping our product claims defensible.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor privacy and data protection developments globally, including GDPR, ePrivacy, CCPA, US state laws, LGPD, PIPEDA, PDPA and emerging regulations; flag relevant items for CookieYes and customers.
  • Write authoritative long‑form content: regulation explainers, jurisdiction guides, compliance checklists, legal update posts and whitepapers.
  • Act as the legal accuracy reviewer for marketing and product content, adhering to an agreed turnaround SLA.
  • Structure content for AI search, AI Overviews and answer engines; collaborate with SEO and AI search team on generative engine optimisation, schema and citation‑worthy formatting.
  • Translate regulatory obligations into product requirements, working with product and engineering on consent, records and disclosures.
  • Support customer‑facing compliance queries escalated by sales and support; build internal reference material to reduce escalations.
  • Review and maintain our own legal documents, including privacy policy, terms of service, DPAs and vendor agreements, with external counsel as needed.
  • Prepare briefing notes for leadership when regulatory changes affect roadmap or positioning.
  • Represent CookieYes publicly through bylined articles, webinars and industry commentary.

Requirements

  • LLB or equivalent law degree from a recognised institution; bar council enrolment welcome but not required.
  • 2+ years of relevant experience in a law firm, in‑house legal team, compliance function or legal publishing role.
  • Demonstrable writing ability for non‑lawyer audiences (publish work, blog, newsletter, etc.).
  • Ability to write for business owners, delivering accuracy without legalese.
  • Working familiarity with data protection law or proven ability to master a regulatory area quickly.
  • Fluency with AI tools for research, drafting and summarisation, with disciplined verification of citations.
  • Strong research discipline: cite primary sources, verify guidance currency, avoid reliance on secondary summaries.
  • Sound judgement distinguishing legal explanation from legal advice.

Good to Have

  • Privacy certification (CIPP/E, CIPP/US, CIPM) or intent to pursue one (support provided).
  • Experience at a SaaS, privacy‑tech or legal‑tech company.
  • Experience drafting or negotiating DPAs and SaaS agreements.
  • Comfort with SEO, GEO and legal content performance in traditional and AI search.
  • Additional language abilities relevant to EU jurisdictions.
  • Deep understanding of major global privacy laws (GDPR, CCPA, DPA, PDPA, UCPA, etc.).

Application
